review.reason:
Select candidate 38 without geometry edits, based on the numbered previews and authoritative hazard facts.

Hole 1: The dry 332-yard par 4 offers a meaningful choice between following the right-turning fairway and attempting a shorter line across collision trees. Three substantial fairway bunkers complicate placement around the bend, while the compact green and flanking/back sand demand a controlled approach. The shortcut is not a free reward; the wider lower fairway provides a credible conservative staging area.

Hole 2: The dry 217-yard par 3 contrasts strongly with the opener. Its generous green, unobstructed front and predominantly back-left/back-right bunkering support conservative center/front targeting rather than requiring an attack on the front-right pin. The separate foreground fairway provides useful short-miss space, although reaching the green still requires a substantial shot.

Hole 3: The 472-yard par 5 has one substantial, elongated right-side lake, not scattered ponds. The broad fairway preserves a safe left-center route, while pursuing distance beside the shoreline brings water into play. The lake ends before the green; greenside sand on both sides rewards a controlled second shot or a deliberate layup rather than imposing a final forced water carry.

The par-4/3/5 sequence, wooded bend, long one-shot target and reachable shoreline finish provide excellent within-round contrast. Recent rounds already include short doglegs and reachable par 5s, limiting novelty, but the right-turning opener and long dry par 3 provide sufficient change without another frequently repeated island green. Simulated 2/1/2 shots to green and 54/51/70 safe tee options support fairness; the visible landing areas independently look playable. Artwork correspondence remains to be reviewed after generation.
